description.narrative:
New Narratives overall goal is to strengthen local independent journalism in Liberia to actively contribute as part of a whole-of-society effort to combat corruption and support good governance and human rights.
New Narratives are proposing to make a slight change to their first objective to reflect the new activities focused on War and Economic Crimes Court reporting. The overall goal continues to be to strengthen local independent journalism in Liberia to actively contribute as part of a whole-of-society effort to combat corruption and support good governance and human rights.
With the new outcome, two main outcomes are expected to be achieved by the intervention:
1) Liberian journalists are equipped with resources, know-how and support, including through strong relationships with relevant non-media CSOs, to pursue independent and investigative journalism during and after the project,including on the war and economics crimes courts.
2) Liberian news organizations and New Narratives have the resources and know-how to enhance financial viability in a sustainable way to support investigative journalism.
This will be achieved by the following broad activities, thoroughly outlined in the proposal, which each include a number of different outputs to promote and boost a sustainable investigative journalism ecosystem by:
a) Building strong investigative and independent journalism capacity; b) Building trusted news organizations with large reach and sustainable, independent revenue; c) Strengthening civil society collaborations; d) Offer investigative journalism grants to journalists at the concerned newsrooms

Insatsen syftar till att stärka självständig and kvalitativ journalistik i Liberia, genom att möjliggöra för New Narratives att bistå med stipendier till journalister och kapacitets bygga liberianska mediahus. New Narratives kommer stötta nyhetsredaktioner med kapacitetsstärkning, journalist-stipendier och kompetensförstärkning fokuserat på digital mediaproduktion och företagsutvecklande. Programmet syftar till att utrusta liberianska journalister och nyhetsredaktioner med resurser, know-how och stöd för att kunna bedriva självständig och grävande journalistik.

The contribution appraised here aims to strengthen independent and qualitative journalism in Liberia by supporting New Narratives to provide production grants to journalists and capacity build Liberian media houses. New Narratives will target newsrooms, with capacity building, journalism-grants and skills strengthening focused on digital media production and business support. The programme aims to equip Liberian journalists and news organisations with the resources, know-how and support to pursue independent and investigative reporting.

description.narrative:
In addition to the examples provided in the latest CoP (UM2022/10343/MONR78) observations on New Narrative's impact was noted during a partner visit to Lofa and Gbarnga in May 2025 such as women's space in media At first, I didnt feel safe, but NN has strengthened me. Im an independent journalist now I run my own budget and make my own decisions and the reallife impact of the reporting when decision makers act on issues reported, or survivors finally feel seen from the War Crimes reporting, see Travel report UM2022/10343/MONR74 for more details.
New Narratives were given a cost extension in November 2024 and has since continued to show impressive results. With the additional funds they have been able to increase their reporting on War Crimes, and train journalists on how to report on the coming War and Economic Crimes Court, as well as explore new models for financial sustainability. Since the signing of the extension New Narratives have already organised workshops for local journalists across the country on how to do informed, critical and trauma sensitive reporting on the War and Economic Crimes Court. These trainings have led to panel debates organised on radio in all counties, with experts present provided by New Narratives. During the abovementioned trip to Lofa the Embassy experienced firsthand how New Narratives reporting on war crimes has a significant impact on survivors. In Zorzor in rural Lofa, the team from the Embassy met with the local commissioner and some traditional leaders who were in his office. The meeting was organised as a part of the protocol, but when there a spontaneous conversation around the work of New Narratives came about since they were a part of the mission. All present at the meeting had heard their reporting on the local radio station, and a Paramount Chief stated how important it has been for him personally to hear about how the chase for accountability continues. He described how his son was brutally killed during the war, he was boiled alive in oil We could only bury his heart, and how he still suffers from this The people who killed my own children are gone without punishment. For him, New Narratives reporting on the trials abroad has brought him sense of justice, and in his eyes the attention serves as both justice and as a deterrent. During the last few months there has also been some significant developments in terms of finding new business models and financially sustainable solutions for the local media outlets. New Narratives have been encouraged by the Embassy to pilot and be experimental when trying to find models that work in the Liberian context, and the developments in the last few months have by far been the most successful so far. New Narratives are focusing their support on developing Frontpage Africa (Liberias biggest newspaper) online presence and to identify potential revenue streams for them. They have brought in a team of two consultant as well as some interns, who have supported Frontpage in setting up a Whatsapp channel and start producing video content. Although New Narratives have not yet reported on the reach and impact, the writing PO notes that the video content is already being widely spread on social media. Since this has been so successful, the Embassy and New Narratives have had some short initial conversations about exploring possibilities to expand the support to other news outlets, primarily radio stations. This would be especially important since the Internews contribution has not managed to create any sustainable financial solutions for ALICOR or their member stations.
